Keeping this in one place means every rule that is keyed by an owner's region reads 27 * the same city-to-region mapping, so they can never drift apart: the region a city 28 * derives here is the region every region-keyed rule sees for that city. 29 * 30 *

A city not listed in the table has no known region and resolves to 31 * {@link #UNKNOWN_REGION}. 32 */ 33 @Component 34 public class CityRegionResolver { 35 36 /** The region returned for a city that is not in the fixed {@link #CITY_REGION} table. */ 37 public static final String UNKNOWN_REGION = "UNKNOWN"; 38 39 /** Fixed city-to-region table; a city not listed here has no known region. */ 40 private static final Map CITY_REGION = Map.of( 41 "Sydney", "NSW", 42 "Melbourne", "VIC", 43 "Brisbane", "QLD"); 44 45 /** Fixed region-to-postcode range table (inclusive 4-digit low/high), keyed by region; a 46 * region not listed here (i.e. {@link #UNKNOWN_REGION}) accepts any 4-digit postcode. */ 47 private static final Map REGION_POSTCODE_RANGE = Map.of( 48 "NSW", new int[] {2000, 2099}, 49 "VIC", new int[] {3000, 3099}, 50 "QLD", new int[] {4000, 4099}); 51 52 /** 53 * Resolve a city to its canonical region. 54 * 55 * @param city the owner's city, as stored 56 * @return the region the city belongs to, or {@link #UNKNOWN_REGION} when the city is 57 * not in the fixed table 58 */ 59 public String regionFor(String city) { 60 return CITY_REGION.getOrDefault(city, UNKNOWN_REGION); 61 } 62 63 /** 64 * Whether a 4-digit {@code postcode} is valid for the given {@code city}. The postcode is 65 * checked against the inclusive range of the city's region (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, 66 * QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. 67 * 68 * @param city the owner's city, as stored 69 * @param postcode a 4-digit postcode string (e.g. '2000') 70 * @return {@code true} if the postcode is within the city's region range, or the city has 71 * no known region; {@code false} if the postcode is out of range for the region 72 */ 73 public boolean isPostcodeValidForCity(String city, String postcode) { 74 int[] range = REGION_POSTCODE_RANGE.get(regionFor(city)); 75 if (range == null) { 76 return true; 77 } 78 int value = Integer.parseInt(postcode); 79 return value >= range[0] && value <= range[1]; 80 } 81 } 82

## Summary

I implemented postcode-preferred locality derivation:

**`CityRegionResolver.java`** — added an overload `regionFor(String city, String postcode)` that looks up the region by postcode range first, falling back to the city table:
- New private `regionForPostcode(postcode)` scans the existing `REGION_POSTCODE_RANGE` table (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099) and returns the matching region, or `null` when the postcode is absent, blank, non-numeric, or in no known range.
- `regionFor(city, postcode)` returns the postcode-derived region when present, otherwise delegates to the existing `regionFor(city)` (which returns `UNKNOWN` for unlisted cities).
- The original single-arg `regionFor` and `isPostcodeValidForCity` are untouched, so validation behavior is unchanged.

**`OwnerMapper.java`** — `locality(owner)` now calls `regionFor(owner.getCity(), owner.getPostcode())` instead of city-only.

This returns the same region for known cities with matching postcodes (e.g. Sydney/2000 → NSW) while disambiguating via postcode — an unknown city with postcode 3000 now resolves to VIC, exactly as the two new acceptance tests assert.
